lines.t: A kiss can cover a motive.
A lie can borrow a voice.
He knows the difference.
Kiss on the cheek, lie underneath,
He knows what a greeting keeps.
Still loves His own, still receives
When we return
Kiss on the cheek, lie underneath,
Nothing gets past what He sees.
Never lost one who belongs
His love was real all along.
No disguise. (He knows.)
No surprise. (He knows.)
Come back honest—
No rehearsed lines.
Judas brought a kiss to a betrayal—
Affection on the surface, underneath it was a sale.
Close enough to greet Him, far enough to plot,
A familiar face doesn't mean a faithful heart.
Some stood in the flock with a different intention,
He read the whole sentence, not just the presentation.
Smile had manners, motive had a price,
Betrayal dressed polite is betrayal twice.
But His love for His own isn't built on their performance,
He doesn't need perfection to recognize belonging.
Never lost one—let the weight of that settle,
His knowing runs deeper than a temporary wrestle.
Nothing hidden in the welcome.
Nothing hidden in the wound.
He knows every contradiction—
Still receives those who return.
Kiss on the cheek, lie underneath,
He knows what a greeting keeps.
Still loves His own, still receives—
When we return
Kiss on the cheek, lie underneath,
Nothing gets past what He sees.
Never lost one who belongs—
His love was real all along.
No disguise. (He knows.)
No surprise. (He knows.)
Come back honest—
No rehearsed lines.
A thought isn't true just because it sounds familiar,
A lie can use a person's own voice to sound sincere.
Repeat it long enough, it starts renting out the memory,
Then calls itself a fact with a counterfeit identity.
Outside pressure, inside persuasion,
A dozen bad conclusions from a little information.
He knows where it started, knows what it became,
Knows the one deceived isn't merely a mistake.
No need to clean the story till the facts look flattering,
A polished explanation doesn't change what happened.
Return means turn—not rename the behavior,
Mercy isn't fooled, and love isn't a waiver.
Yet no one coming back gets rejected at reception,
No performance needed, no perfected recollection.
He knows the whole account before the first admission—
His welcome isn't ignorance; He knows and still receives them.
Love doesn't call betrayal harmless.
Truth doesn't need a disguise.
Mercy doesn't mean He missed it—
He received them with open arms
Known in the failure.
Loved through the doubt.
Return without the cover—
Nothing edited out.
Kiss on the cheek, lie underneath,
He knows what a greeting keeps.
Still loves His own, still receives—
When we return
Kiss on the cheek, lie underneath,
Nothing gets past what He sees.
Never lost one who belongs—
His love was real all along.
No disguise.
No rehearsed lines.
He knows the difference—
And He knows His own.
